title: Active_Crisis.bundle is a compaction-prone slot index — a topology edit that removes an earlier-ordered bundle renumbers slots mid-crisis, emitting a spurious Crisis_Resolved + re-Trigger for a flaw that never cleared (E13 dedup breach) or silently re-binding the crisis to a different bundle
evidence:
core/types.odin:224 — "bundle:        u32, // Saturated_Bundle: the bottleneck bundle slot (NO_BUNDLE otherwise)"

core/bundles.odin:106-113 — "// reset the bundle rows (a topology change can drop/reshape bundles; rebuild
// from scratch — correctness over incremental churn at this scale)
clear(&b.bundle_lo)
clear(&b.bundle_hi)
clear(&b.bundle_cap)
clear(&b.bundle_count)
clear(&b.bundle_tier)
b.n = 0" (slots re-minted in pipe-slot scan order; "bs = b.n" for each new pair)

core/step.odin:84-86 — "if state.topology.gen != state.bundles_gen {
	bundles_rebuild(&state.bundles, &state.topology, cat)
	state.bundles_gen = state.topology.gen
}" (runs before crisis_evaluate in the same step)

core/crisis.odin:283-285 — "relieved := bound > 0 &&
	bundle_class_queue(state, cat, ac.bundle, ac.class) + margin < bound &&
	!bundle_lane_at_bound(state, cat, ac.bundle)" (the resolve predicate measures the stored slot against the rebuilt table; no re-validation that the slot still names the trigger-time pair — bundle_class_queue/bundle_lane_count match packets by CURRENT pipe_bundle slot)
detail: Trigger on slot k; player demolishes any earlier-ordered pair mid-crisis; rebuild shifts the named pair to k-1. Resolve measures dead/renamed slot k: queue 0 → relieved → Crisis_Resolved while the named queue is still at the E9 bound, then same-tick re-Trigger — violating the pinned 'While ACTIVE, the condition is never re-emitted' and 'exactly one Crisis_Triggered per activation'. If slot k re-binds to another saturated pair, banner/outline silently name the wrong bundle. All shipped tests edit only the named bundle itself; no test removes an unrelated earlier pair.
recommended_fix: Key the active row on the stable pair identity (bundle_lo/bundle_hi node ids at trigger) or the stable member pipe id, re-resolving the current slot; add a test demolishing an earlier-ordered pair while the crisis is active.

title: Pool_Exhaustion trigger is class-filtered but the frozen contract says 'any Pool_Exhaustion drop' — with QoS reprioritization the pool crisis never fires while the surge pins the pool at cap
detail: If the surge arrival rides a higher-priority lane than residents (QoS lanes are player-engineered), every pool shed pays a resident class, so no surge-class Pool_Exhaustion event ever exists — the map-wide backstop never fires while the surge keeps the pool at cap and shedding every tick, contradicting the frozen 'any drop' contract.
recommended_fix: Match the frozen contract: accept any Pool_Exhaustion drop this tick (drop the class filter for the pool cause only), or amend the frozen spec text with a documented deviation and a covering test.

title: Empty-string or wrong-typed archetype_id silently loads as a pure demand event (archetype_idx = -1) instead of the fail-fast the catalog-validation contract pins for unknown refs
detail: "archetype_id": "" or "archetype_id": 5 is indistinguishable from an absent field — the set-piece loads clean and silently never fires a crisis, while a non-empty unknown id fails fast ("unknown archetype_id %q"). A typo'd deletion of the id silently disables the story's crisis.
recommended_fix: Reject a PRESENT but empty/wrong-typed archetype_id (fail-fast like unknown ids), e.g. check key presence separately from jstr's value.

title: Set-piece index truncates to u16 in the dedup key and serialized row but demand.json has no set-piece count cap (the crises roster got a 255 cap for exactly this payload-truncation reason)
detail: With ≥65536 set pieces in one era, si truncates: two set pieces share a dedup key and Crisis_Resolved/Triggered rows + the banner's set-piece name (de.set_pieces[ac.set_piece].id) attribute the wrong activation. Pathological data, but the codebase pattern is fail-fast caps.
recommended_fix: Cap era set_pieces at load (≤ 65535, mirroring the crises 255 cap rationale) or widen set_piece to u32 in Active_Crisis and the serialized row.

title: test_crisis_replay_identity discards crisis_record_run's events return value, leaking the [dynamic]Event buffer under the tracking allocator
evidence:
core/crisis_test.odin:53 — "events := make([dynamic]Event, 0, 8)"

core/crisis_test.odin:370 — "hashes, _ := crisis_record_run(&s, 2400, cat)" (inside the run closure; the returned events dynamic is never deleted)

odin test core output — "<      512B/  52.83KiB> <  44.87KiB> (   90/   92) :: core.test_crisis_replay_identity
        +++ leak       256B @ 0x487806028 [crisis_test.odin:53:crisis_record_run()]
        +++ leak       256B @ 0x48780B720 [crisis_test.odin:53:crisis_record_run()]"
detail: Each run() invocation leaks the cap-8 events array (256B, twice). Every other crisis test defers delete(evs); this one discards it. Harmless now, but the project's tracking-allocator discipline treats leaks as failures; the new test code should be clean.
recommended_fix: Capture and delete the discarded return: "hashes, evs := crisis_record_run(...); defer delete(evs)" in the run closure.
